On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 8:23 AM Anna Bright <anna.bright@brightlayer.com> wrote:
> We ran into an issue during our month-end remittance: a $12,400 credit from payment ref BL-20270401 appears applied to the wrong legal entity in your ledger (Redwood Inc. US vs Redwood EMEA).

Thanks Anna — I reviewed the posting. Looks like the payment landed in our US AR clearing (GL 1200-AR-CLEAR) and our auto-apply rule matched the larger outstanding invoice (BL-4413). BL-4412 is registered to Redwood EMEA (entity code RDEU) so the system couldn't auto-apply across entities.

Quick proposed approach (to avoid revenue recognition impact):
1) Create an intercompany JV to move USD 7,600 from US AR clearing to EMEA AR clearing.
   - Debit 1200-AR-CLEAR (US) USD 7,600
   - Credit 2100-INTERCOMP-RECEIVABLE (US) USD 7,600
2) On EMEA books, mirror entry to credit 1200-AR-CLEAR-EU and debit 2100-INTERCOMP-PAYABLE so BL-4412 is marked paid.
3) Post reversing entries for the intercompany offset at the start of next reporting period (2027-05-01) to avoid long-term misstatements.

I attached a CSV with the proposed JV rows and the affected AR refs (proposed_journal_entries_20270420.csv). If legal needs to accept this path, fine — otherwise we can take the alternative of issuing a contra application and credit memo plus recharge, but that increases operational overhead.

Grace: confirm there are no revenue mapping flags for BL-4412 once we do the intercompany move (it should be net-neutral on revenue).

M.
